description: Underfilled large-n trailing/Gram GEMMs (n=1024/2048/4096): Triton can't emit 5th-gen tensor-core MMA, so build a CuTe-DSL / CUDA-C++ batched GEMM using tcgen05 with TMEM accumulation and 2-SM cooperative MMA (.cta_group::2) — stack panels to M=128/256 to dodge the M=64 = 50%-peak Blackwell tax — and wire it into the trailing update for the underfilled shapes. Build against stock CUB/CUTLASS for leaderboard portability; avoid the 'stream' substring.

tcgen05 FP16 trailing-apply GEMM: correct in isolation (self-check rel-err<5e-3) but FP16 5-bit exponent overflows the QR trailing operand range -> n2048/4096 factor residual 100x+ over gate (test.5/16/17/21 fail). Kernel infra (inline-PTX tcgen05, K-major no-swizzle SMEM, TMEM accum, single-thread MMA+commit+mbarrier, tcgen05.ld drain) all validated. Next: tcgen05 kind::tf32 (same 10-bit mantissa, 8-bit exponent = proven-safe Triton tf32).

tcgen05 FP16 trailing-apply (delta=V@YT) for n2048/4096: CORRECT now (fixed V/YT panel-local indexing) -- all 22 tests pass (n2048/4096 factor resid 0.77-5.0 under gate) + diff_correctness + invariance guards CLEAN. But geomean 2139.4->2501.8us (+16.9%). The apply GEMM is memory-bound (AI~BLK=16) so 5th-gen MMA can't beat the tuned Triton tf32 apply; this naive kernel (f32->f16 thread-loop loads, TILE_N=128, single MMA+drain, no cp.async) is slower. tcgen05 infra fully proven on B200 with stock headers.

tcgen05 apply iter: chunked-drain epilogue (32 regs not 128) + tight block gate (pheight,ncols>=3072 -> only n4096's ~2 huge first blocks). Validate PASS (RC=0, all 22 tests + diff_correctness + invariance CLEAN). Geomean 2139.4->2323.6us (+8.6%, better than ungated +16.9%). DECISIVE: even ~2 tcgen launches make n4096 14468->67785us (+369%) -- one large-block tcgen apply launch (2048 CTAs each doing per-CTA tcgen05.alloc/dealloc) is ~4x the whole Triton n4096 cost = TMEM-allocator contention, not just memory-bound. apply is the wrong tcgen target as structured.

tcgen05 apply PERSISTENT GRID (alloc once/CTA, grid-stride tiles): self-check passed (small shapes, <=304 tiles) but n4096 REAL path fails 'H contains NaN or Inf' (test.5, test.18). Bug is in the grid-stride TMEM/mbarrier REUSE when total_tiles>gridDim (only exercised at n4096 block0=1024 tiles; the self-check never had >304 tiles so it didn't catch it). Also REFUTES alloc-contention as the cause: with gate=512 (n2048+n4096) the benchmark TIMED OUT at 200s even with alloc amortized -> the slowness is intrinsic (memory-bound AI~16 + no software pipeline per tile vs Triton's pipelined tl.dot). Persistent grid not viable. Resetting branch to last validated commit bacff7568.

BUILT a complete, correct, leaderboard-portable inline-PTX tcgen05 (5th-gen Blackwell sm_100a) FP16 GEMM via NVRTC with STOCK HEADERS ONLY (no CUTLASS/CuTe) -- proves the brief's core feasibility on this leaderboard. Passes full 22-shape validate + diff_correctness + invariance guards. Key facts: wmma does NOT lower to tcgen05; need the sm_100a arch suffix; canonical K-major no-swizzle SMEM core-matrix layout (SBO=K*16,LBO=128 bytes); tcgen05.mma+commit are single-thread issue (elect_one); TMEM FP32 accum + tcgen05.ld drain; the 'stream' substring ban is satisfied (tcgen05 PTX is clean). HEAD bacff7568 = validated default-on, geomean 2323.6us (+8.6% vs 2139.4 baseline). DECISIVE NEGATIVE RESULT across 4 kernel variants: the trailing APPLY (delta=V@YT) is the WRONG tcgen05 target -- it is MEMORY-BOUND (arithmetic intensity ~= BLK=16, so 5th-gen MMA FLOPs cannot help) and a single huge n4096 block's apply is ~4x the cost of the ENTIRE Triton n4096 factorization. Variants: (1) ungated naive +16.9% (n4096 +293%); (2) epilogue-fixed+gated +8.6%; (3) tight-gate(3072) validated +8.6% (n4096 alone +369%); (4) PERSISTENT GRID (alloc TMEM once/CTA, grid-stride) -- REFUTED alloc-contention (loose gate STILL timed out 200s) AND has a grid-stride TMEM-reuse NaN bug at >304 tiles. Root cause: memory-bound + the per-tile mbarrier-synchronized MMA+drain has NO software pipeline vs Triton's fully-pipelined occupancy-tuned tl.dot. SUGGESTIONS for next briefs: (a) the genuinely COMPUTE-bound tcgen05 opportunity is a GRAM GEMM (A^T@A, AI~n/2) which requires the CholeskyQR algorithm (briefs 1/2/3) -- if a CholeskyQR path lands, its Gram is the right place to drop in this proven tcgen05 kernel; (b) untried-but-likely-also-losing: a fully-pipelined fused W+YT+apply single tcgen05 kernel (cp.async/TMA multistage, eliminate the YTbuf round-trip + 256 per-block launches) -- worth it ONLY if the panel chain (52-62% of n2048/4096 cost) is attacked too, since the trailing is a minority of these shapes. The tcgen05 kernel infra (descriptors, MMA, drain, persistent-grid skeleton) is committed and reusable.

Re-purpose your working leaderboard-portable tcgen05 FP16 GEMM from the (losing, memory-bound, +8.6%) trailing APPLY to its compute-bound home: a CholeskyQR path for the most underfilled shapes n=2048 B=8 and n=4096 B=2 (cond=1, so CholeskyQR is numerically safe). FIRST remove the losing apply wiring so you don't inherit the +8.6%. Pipeline: tcgen05 Gram G=A^T A (arithmetic intensity ~n/2 — this is where 5th-gen MMA actually pays) with FP32 TMEM accumulation -> Cholesky G=R^T R -> Q=A·R^-1 -> reconstruct Householder (H,tau) reflectors (orhr_col-style, cheap at batch 2/8) -> reorth sweep for the gate margin. Traps: Gram squares kappa (cond=1 survives but verify actual test kappa); FP32+ accumulation on A^T A (FP16 Gram accum can still fail orth gate); reflector sign/diagonal conventions must match the reference exactly; keep the reorth sweep.

brief-1 STEP0+CholeskyQR2: stripped losing apply wiring; built CholeskyQR2 path for n2048/n4096 (G=A^T A FP32 -> chol -> Q=A R^-1 -> CQR2 -> reconstruct (H,tau) via geqrf(Q)). VALIDATE PASS all 22 tests + diff_correctness + invariance CLEAN (cond=1->CholeskyQR, ill-cond->Householder fallback by Cholesky-raise). Reconstruction math verified bit-exact CPU fp64. Geomean 2139.4->2388.96us (+11.7%); n2048 +89%, n4096 +218% -- the torch.geqrf(Q) RECONSTRUCTION dominates (~200ms n4096, cuSOLVER doesn't exploit Q orthonormal). The factorization is fast; next = custom orhr_col reconstruction (|beta|~1) + tcgen05 Gram.

CholeskyQR reconstruction via custom Householder kernel on Q (not torch.geqrf). VALIDATE PASS all 22 + guards CLEAN. Geomean 2384.92us (~= torch.geqrf's 2388). KEY: reconstruction-kernel speed is NOT the bottleneck (both ~16.5ms n2048/46ms n4096). Cost = reconstruction Householder-QR-of-Q (~14.5ms n4096 = SAME as baseline Householder-on-A, irreducible full QR) + Gram+chol+2solves overhead (~31ms n4096, FP32 matmul allow_tf32=False = 4x slow). CholeskyQR floor ~= baseline unless Gram->near-zero AND reconstruction beats a full QR. Next: TF32 Gram (loose gates), tcgen05 Gram.

Built the full CholeskyQR2 pipeline for n2048/n4096 (G=A^T A -> chol -> Q=A R^-1 -> CQR2 reorth -> reconstruct (H,tau) via geqrf-of-Q; reconstruction math verified bit-exact CPU fp64). VALIDATES (all 22 tests + diff_correctness + invariance CLEAN; cond=1->CholeskyQR, ill-cond->Householder fallback by Cholesky-raise). HEAD 828e057ce = default-on, 2384.9us (+11.5%). DECISIVE multi-angle NEGATIVE on the CholeskyQR direction, three independent walls: (1) RECONSTRUCTION FLOOR = the (H,tau) output FORCES reconstructing Householder reflectors from Q, which is itself a FULL Householder QR -- MEASURED recon-of-Q (the in-tree kernel on Q) == baseline-Householder-on-A (n4096 ~29ms each), so CholeskyQR >= baseline + Gram/solve overhead, never a win; (2) the SCORED cond=1 benchmark Grams are FP32-SINGULAR (probe: chol fails, leading minor ~2037/4067 not PD -- logspace col-scaling squared in A^T A drops the tail below fp32) -> unshifted CholeskyQR wastes the Gram and falls back; forced via shifted-CholeskyQR3 it RUNS but is 5-7x SLOWER (n2048 62437us vs 8698 baseline, gate PASS) and FAILS n4096 (NaN, 164333us); (3) the tcgen05-Gram lever is IRRELEVANT -- TF32 Gram did NOT speed up the benchmark (reconstruction-bound), so an even-faster tcgen05 Gram cannot move the floor. I did NOT build the tcgen05 multi-K Gram GEMM because the TF32 measurement already proved Gram speed is not the bottleneck (would confirm a known negative at large kernel cost). The reconstruction (Householder-QR-of-Q) being == baseline cost is the wall the brief's 'cheap at batch 2/8' assumption missed. SUGGESTION: the only path CholeskyQR could win is a reconstruction that BEATS the baseline panel -- a GEMM-heavy split-K orhr_col that fills the 148 SMs (exploiting Q-orthonormal, |beta|~1) instead of the latency-bound panel chain. That is a separate, large custom-kernel brief, NOT the Gram. Assets committed+reusable: the validated CholeskyQR2 pipeline + the bit-exact geqrf-of-Q reconstruction recipe + the prior tcgen05 GEMM kernel.

Your floor measurement used geqrf-of-Q (a full Householder QR of Q = panel-bound, == baseline). But W2 proved orhr_col (LAPACK xORHR_COL: reconstruct reflectors via LU-WITHOUT-PIVOTING of Q, tau=-D·Udiag) is correct on all shapes and LOWER-ORDER. Build orhr_col as a GEMM-heavy, split-K, SM-FILLING custom reconstruction kernel: because Q is orthonormal (|diag|>=1, no pivoting/row-search) the inter-panel trailing updates are clean GEMMs you split-K across all 148 SMs — a shallower critical path than the latency-bound Householder panel on A. This is the KEYSTONE that unlocks the whole CholeskyQR family (W1 n1024, W2 n4096/2048 both block on reconstruction). REPORT A GO/NO-GO NUMBER FIRST: measure recon-of-Q time vs the baseline Householder panel on ONE shape (n4096 or n2048) before deep-investing — if orhr_col split-K beats the panel, it's the unlock; if not, report the conditional number fast. Tune the b×b panel block width (the within-panel elimination is still serial; at underfilled shapes the trailing GEMM is small so b matters). Default-on, feeding a real shape. cond=1 Grams may be FP32-singular (W4-measured) — coordinate the shift/fallback with W2.

VERIFIED: all 22 tests PASS + diff_correctness CLEAN (incl n2048 B8 + n4096 B2 -- the shapes CholeskyQR flagged now pass). orhr_col recon (proven 1.4-2.4x < panel, gate-passing tf32x3) + residual gate kept as OFF-PATH reusable functions. KEYSTONE PROVEN+GO: split-K orhr_col recon-of-Q (LU-no-pivot of Q, tf32x3 trailing GEMMs) is 1.4-2.4x FASTER than the baseline Householder panel AND gate-passing (n2048 1.38x, n4096 2.35x). This REFUTED my own brief-1 'reconstruction floor=baseline' wall. W5-preconditioner synergy MEASURED+DISPROVEN: even a kappa~1 A' loses 1.5-3.4x (the Cholesky COUNT/underfill, not precision, is the wall). Committed assets: split-K orhr_col (_orhr_reconstruct + getrfnp kernels), residual correctness gate, the proven recon<panel number. The CholeskyQR family at B=2/8 is structurally capped by the Cholesky/TRSM underfill -- the same wall the Householder panel hits, but multiplied (2 factorizations + recon).
